key_idea: After Floyd-Warshall on the directed road graph, cost[product][warehouse] is a plain sum, and choosing m distinct warehouses for m products is a min-cost assignment (Hungarian).
sketch: Read the directed distance matrix (-1 = no road), run Floyd-Warshall in O(n^3). cost[p][w] = sum over warehouses j of amount[j][p]*dist(j,w), O(n^2 m). Solve the rectangular m x n assignment with the O(m n^2) Hungarian algorithm with potentials. Pitfalls: roads are directed and asymmetric (goods move from source j to target w), the input matrix line j gives distances from j, and totals reach about 1e11 so use 64-bit.
